non_blocking_notes: ROUND-1 REQUIRED CHANGE VERIFIED APPLIED. The revised m1-s1 summary no longer contains the falsified claim that br_ana and no_nve expose offline committed-fixture generation paths, and no longer instructs re-running the thirteen generate_catalogue.py entry points for the artifacts. It now specifies reading each committed artifact and performing only an in-place, value-preserving column rename preserving every row, value, null, Date dtype, column position and last_catalogue_check. That route is genuinely offline: it touches no network and no generator entry point. The replacement justification is itself measured true — `git ls-tree -r --name-only 4b16c57 -- src | grep -E 'native.parquet|station_products.parquet'` returns thirteen station_products.parquet and only eleven native.parquet, with none under br_ana/ or no_nve/, and the committed fixtures tests/test_data/br_ana_metadata.json and no_nve_metadata.json are JSON lists of 4 and 3 stations against packaged artifacts of 52,145 and 44,001 rows. The second half of the justification is also true: `git grep -n 'last_catalogue_check":' 4b16c57 -- src/rivretrieve/_internal/providers` shows br_ana:264, fr_hubeau:728 and :745, jp_mlit:251, no_nve:326, pl_imgw:411 and za_dws:346 writing the caller-supplied catalogue_date, so a re-run would mutate a published column the step promises to preserve.

ROUND-2 SWEEP — the thirteen row counts were measured, not trusted, by reading the parquet files with pyarrow: ba_fhmzbih 180, br_ana 52145, ca_eccc 16114, ch_foen 738, cz_chmi 4155, fr_hubeau 33139, jp_mlit 4092, lt_lhmt 194, no_nve 44001, pl_imgw 3903, th_thaiwater 1650, usgs_nwis 157548, za_dws 8715. Every figure matches the graph's stated list in provider order exactly, with no material difference. Thirteen files were found by glob, matching the stated thirteen.

ROUND-2 SWEEP — the eight-column-order claim measured true. Every one of the thirteen artifacts carries exactly ['provider_id','station_id','product_id','availability','availability_reason','start_date','end_date','last_catalogue_check'], and start_date/end_date are date32[day] in all thirteen, matching the pl.Date declaration at src/rivretrieve/_internal/catalogues/schemas.py:72-73 and the eight CatalogueColumn entries of STATION_PRODUCT_CATALOG_SCHEMA at schemas.py:64-79.

ROUND-2 SWEEP — the 'USGS published bounds retain their dates while null-bound providers remain null' claim measured true. Counting non-null start_date per artifact gives 57,450 of 157,548 for usgs_nwis and 0 for all twelve other providers, which matches source: every non-USGS generator writes literal None for both bounds (ba_fhmzbih:340-341, br_ana:262-263, ca_eccc:460-461, ch_foen:235-236, cz_chmi:263-264, fr_hubeau:726-727 and 743-744, jp_mlit:249-250, lt_lhmt:199-200, no_nve:324-325, pl_imgw:409-410, th_thaiwater:460-461, za_dws:344-345), while usgs_nwis:783-784 writes the dates returned by _matching_coverage at :761.

ROUND-2 SWEEP — the named test function exists verbatim. `git grep -n 'def test_all_packaged' 4b16c57 -- tests` returns tests/test_package.py:99 def test_all_packaged_catalogues_expose_exact_reduced_carriers, and reading lines 99-130 shows a loop over a literal thirteen-id tuple asserting `artifact.station_products.schema == STATION_PRODUCT_CATALOG_SCHEMA.polars_schema` at line 126. The co-landing claim therefore holds: renaming the schema without renaming the artifacts, or the reverse, fails this test for all thirteen providers, so the single-node decomposition is not merely convenient but forced.

ROUND-2 SWEEP — the do-not-rename boundary re-measured and correct. USGS SERIES_ONLY_FIELDS is defined at usgs_nwis/generate_catalogue.py:250 as SERIES_HEADER[12:], and SERIES_HEADER carries native begin_date/end_date at :131-132, read back by index at :825-826; those are native NWIS field names and must not be renamed, as the step says. ThaiWater's start_date/end_date are URL query parameters and appear only in tests/test_internal_window_planning.py:73-74 and :186-187 (and in the untracked-by-src reference/legacy_observations tree), not in src — so the step's exclusion names real occurrences. driver.py:63-64,70,76 carries requested_start_date/requested_end_date, already prefixed and not bare. ADR-0015 station-level start_date/end_date are removed station fields, a different column, correctly left alone.

ROUND-2 SWEEP — the ADR claims hold. docs/adr/0012-a-catalogue-column-declares-its-origin.md:17 names `start_date`, and docs/adr/0014-catalogue-metadata-is-croissant.md:24 carries the Croissant `{ "@type": "Field", "name": "start_date" ... }` example. Both files are tracked at 4b16c57. No committed Croissant JSON artifact exists under any provider catalogue directory (each holds only native.parquet, products.parquet, provider.json, station_products.parquet, stations.parquet), so there is no packaged metadata file the rename additionally has to touch.

Graph validity clean: one node, id m1-s1 numbered from 1 with no gaps or duplicates, repo exactly "RivRetrieve", depends_on empty. No edge to refute, no cycle, no dangling reference, no edge outside m1. No missing edge is provable because there is only one node and it is atomic by test force. No line-level prescription. No version bump or tag, matching the NONE policy. Nothing from vision Scope-Out is scheduled.
Scope coverage matches m1 and vision Scope-In item 10 exactly: schema, thirteen generators, tests/fixtures, packaged catalogues, and the two binding ADRs. Nothing scheduled here belongs to m2-m9.

Wording note only, not a defect: vision Scope-In item 10 says "the regenerated packaged catalogues", while the revised step updates them by in-place rename. The observable outcome the vision's acceptance criterion demands — published_record_start_date and published_record_end_date present, no bare start_date or end_date surviving in the catalogue schema — is unaffected by which mechanism produces the artifact, and the rename route is the only offline one, so the divergence in the vision's verb is immaterial and needs no vision edit.

Coverage note for the eventual plan writer, not a graph defect: the step's generic clause "update affected fixtures and assertions" has to reach tests/conftest.py:155-156,169-170,179-180,189-190,204-205; tests/test_internal_catalogue_schemas.py:48-49,61-62,93-94,122-123,189-190,199-200; tests/test_internal_packaged_catalogue_artifact.py:97-98,110-111,299-300; tests/test_ch_foen_generate_catalogue.py:387-388; tests/test_fr_hubeau_generate_catalogue.py:1177-1178; tests/test_pl_imgw_generate_catalogue.py:212-213; tests/test_za_dws_generate_catalogue.py:612-613; and the canonical-row assertions in tests/test_usgs_nwis_generate_catalogue.py:514-515,520-521,532-533 — while leaving that same file's native _series_row begin_date/end_date at :54,216,224,493-495 and tests/test_data/usgs_nwis_metadata_series.json untouched. This is enumeration for the plan, not a missing scope item.
summary: The revised graph survives. The round-1 required change was genuinely applied, not restated: the artifact clause now specifies an in-place, value-preserving column rename of the thirteen committed station_products.parquet files and the false br_ana/no_nve committed-fixture feasibility claim is gone, replaced by a justification I measured true (no native.parquet under br_ana or no_nve, fixtures of 4 and 3 stations against 52,145- and 44,001-row artifacts, and catalogue_date-sourced last_catalogue_check in six providers that a re-run would mutate). Every new quantitative claim was measured rather than accepted: all thirteen row counts match the stated list exactly, all thirteen artifacts carry the same eight columns in the stated order with date32[day] bounds, usgs_nwis holds 57,450 non-null start_date values while all twelve other providers hold zero, and tests/test_package.py::test_all_packaged_catalogues_expose_exact_reduced_carriers exists verbatim at tests/test_package.py:99 with the schema-equality assertion at line 126 inside a loop over a literal thirteen-id tuple, which is what genuinely forces schema and artifacts to co-land. The rename/do-not-rename boundary matches the actual occurrence set at the ref, and ADR-0012:17 and ADR-0014:24 really do name these columns. The graph is a single valid node with no edges, no cycle, no out-of-milestone reference, no Scope-Out work and no version bump, and it covers m1's boundary exactly.
